chunks: Three - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who prayed the prayers while in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) for one day, two days, and three days. Then he mentioned after that, he said: 'He purifies himself, gives the adhan, and calls the iqamah for the first one, then prays and calls the iqamah after that for each prayer, so he prays without adhan until he fulfills his prayer.'.
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever misses the Friday prayer, he prays it as four (rak'ahs). That is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.أَوَّلِهِنَّ: The first of them (referring to the first missed prayer)
key_terms.إِقَامُ: The second call to prayer, immediately preceding the start of the prayer
key_terms.الشَّيْخُ: Refers to Al-Shaykh al-Tusi, the author of Tahdhib al-Ahkam
key_terms.الصَّلَوَاتِ: The prayers (specifically the five daily obligatory prayers)
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: Making up a missed obligatory act

ai.seo_question: How does one make up missed prayers if they were in a state of junub?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam details the procedural method for qada (making up) missed obligatory prayers when a person was in a state of major impurity (junub) for consecutive days. It establishes that while the initial purification and full call to prayer (adhan and iqamah) are required for the first missed prayer, subsequent prayers in the sequence only require the iqamah, reflecting a practical easing for the worshipper. The text further clarifies the specific ruling for missed Friday prayer, which is performed as four rak'ahs, distinguishing it from the standard two-rak'ah Friday prayer.
